answer.justification: The patient presents with the classic triad of reactive arthritis (Reiter syndrome): asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee/ankle), conjunctivitis, and urethritis (dysuria), following a gastrointestinal infection (bloody diarrhea). A hallmark clinical feature of reactive arthritis is enthesitis, which is inflammation at the sites where tendons or ligaments insert into bone, most commonly involving the Achilles tendon or plantar fascia.
